title: China's Nuclear Push Meets Southeast Asia's Trust Deficit
text:
China's Nuclear Push Meets Southeast Asia's Trust Deficit

ThinkChina

TPG/Getty Images

The following excerpt is from an article published in ThinkChina on November 4, 2026, written by Kevin Zongzhe Li, Fellow at ASPI's Center for China Analysis (CCA), and Genevieve Donnellon-May, Affiliated Researcher at CCA.China accounts for roughly half of the world’s nuclear reactors currently under construction, but its overseas reactor exports have succeeded only in Pakistan. In Southeast Asia, where Chinese companies already enjoy a substantial presence in clean energy industries, Beijing has yet to secure a commercial reactor construction contract.Disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz have renewed Southeast Asia’s interest in nuclear energy. This presents an opportunity for China to extend its technological and commercial reach in the region. Yet Russia, South Korea and other suppliers are offering competing technologies, financing arrangements and long-term services. As Southeast Asian governments explore their nuclear options, their choice of partners could carry geopolitical implications lasting generations.Read the full article here.
